findings.evidence: Activation checklist, no explanation needed: native props via `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>`, variants as a discriminated union, `children: ReactNode`, an explicit state type when the initializer is `null`, `[]` or one member of a literal union.
findings.fix: Keep only the item the model gets wrong: give `useState` an explicit type when the initializer is `null`, `[]` or one member of a literal union. Drop ComponentPropsWithoutRef, discriminated-union variants and `children: ReactNode`, which current models already write by default.

findings.evidence: React 19 upgrade breaks: ... Before fixing by hand, on a clean git tree run `npx types-react-codemod@3.5.3 preset-19 <dirs>` ... review `git diff`, then typecheck.
findings.fix: Move the ordered migration steps (clean tree, then codemod, then git diff review, then typecheck) out of the Gotchas bullet into a short numbered 'React 19 migration' step in section 1 or 5. Keep only the type-break facts in Gotchas, so the sequence reads as a workflow and not as one of many warnings.

findings.evidence: - Handlers: the submitter and IME Enter traps are in event-handlers.md.
findings.fix: State both traps inline in one line each. Read the submitter from `e.nativeEvent.submitter`, because `currentTarget` is the form. Check `e.nativeEvent.isComposing` before treating Enter as submit. An agent writing a handler without loading event-handlers.md will not know to look for these traps.

findings.evidence: select them at its prompt, run them by name (`npx types-react-codemod@3.5.3 no-implicit-ref-callback-return <dirs>`), or fix those two breaks by hand.
findings.fix: Make one default: after `preset-19`, always run `npx types-react-codemod@3.5.3 no-implicit-ref-callback-return <dirs>` and `npx types-react-codemod@3.5.3 react-element-default-any-props <dirs>` by name. Agents run in non-interactive shells and cannot answer the codemod's selection prompt. Mention fixing by hand only as the fallback when a transform fails.

findings.evidence: "id": "submit-handler" ... assertions: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>, ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>, FormData from e.currentTarget
findings.fix: Replace this eval, whose assertions pass without the skill, with one that exercises a skill-only rule. Example: a form with two submit buttons where the handler must read `e.nativeEvent.submitter`, or an Enter-to-submit input that must ignore IME composition. Add assertions for both.

findings.evidence: Run the project's typecheck script, or `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` when a `tsconfig.json` exists.
findings.fix: Add this branch: if `tsconfig.json` is a solution file (`"files": []` with `references`, as in the Vite react-ts template), `tsc --noEmit -p .` checks nothing and passes silently. Run `npx tsc -b` instead, or `-p` on the referenced app config such as `tsconfig.app.json`. Check that config's `include` when placing `*.type-test.tsx` files in step 3.

findings.evidence: The API table says "first matching row wins" and maps "`react` 18 in `dependencies`" to "React 18-compatible code". For an explicit React 18-to-19 migration in an existing app, this selects the source version instead of the requested target; the requested-major branch only applies when package.json is absent.
findings.fix: Add an explicit migration-target branch before the installed-major rows: when upgrading an app to React 19, update react, react-dom, @types/react and @types/react-dom together, then select React 19 APIs. Preserve React 18 compatibility for published packages whose peer contract still allows 18 unless changing that contract is explicitly requested.

findings.evidence: The Enter-to-send guard is "if (e.key !== 'Enter' || e.shiftKey || e.nativeEvent.isComposing) return". Safari can report isComposing=false for the Enter that commits an IME composition, so this branch can submit the form instead of merely accepting the composed text.
findings.fix: Add the Safari compatibility guard e.nativeEvent.keyCode === 229 alongside isComposing. Add an eval distinguishing IME-confirm Enter, ordinary Enter-to-send and Shift+Enter.
